full_caption: Perrin Dunmoor, Appellant, v. Perrin Fenwicke, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Appellant Perrin Dunmoor is the record owner of the residential building located at 1907 Bellweather Street, Elmsworth, WM, a 4-unit structure operated as rental housing since 1987. Appellee Perrin Fenwicke occupied Unit 1C under a written lease dated January 11, 2022.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A tenant electing to withhold rent under the repair-and-deduct statute must (1) give written notice of the defect, (2) allow a reasonable time for cure, and (3) deposit the withheld sums with the clerk of court or into a segregated account. Perrin Fenwicke satisfied the first two requirements but did not deposit the withheld rent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Perrin Fenwicke withheld rent for the months of June and August of 1998, asserting that the premises were untenantable by reason of a persistent failure of the heating system and recurring water intrusion at the north wall of the unit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The lease provided for monthly rent of $1,575, due on the first day of each month, with a late charge of $50 assessed on any installment remaining unpaid after the 15th day of the month. The trial court found that this charge operated as a penalty rather than as liquidated damages.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The record establishes that Perrin Dunmoor received written notice of the heating defect on October 24, 2013 and did not dispatch a repair contractor until March 21, 2025, an interval of 14 days. During that interval overnight interior temperatures fell below fifty-five degrees on at least eleven occasions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The implied warranty of habitability is not waivable by lease term. Any provision purporting to require a tenant to accept the premises 'as is' is void as against the public policy of this State insofar as it reaches conditions materially affecting health and safety.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Perrin Dunmoor served a notice to quit on August 4, 2020. The notice recited the ground of non-payment but omitted the amount claimed to be due. A notice to quit that fails to state the sum demanded does not commence the statutory cure period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The security deposit of $2,800 was not returned within 30 days of surrender, nor was an itemized statement of deductions furnished. The statutory consequence is forfeiture of the landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: A late fee is enforceable only where it bears a reasonable relationship to the administrative cost actually incurred by the landlord in processing a delinquent payment. A charge of $50 against a monthly obligation of $1,575 exceeds that relationship and is unenforceable to the extent it exceeds five percent of the installment.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Retaliatory eviction is presumed where a landlord commences a summary possession action within 18 months after a tenant has reported a code violation to the municipal housing inspector. The presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence of an independent, non-retaliatory ground.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: We affirm in part and reverse in part. The judgment of possession is vacated; the money judgment is remanded for recalculation consistent with the late-fee holding set out above.

sections.heading: RIDER B — HABITABILITY, REPAIRS AND ACCESS
sections.text: Landlord shall maintain the heating, plumbing, electrical and structural elements of the Premises in good and safe working order. Tenant shall give Landlord written notice of any condition requiring repair. Landlord shall commence a repair affecting heat, hot water, or sanitation within twenty-four (24) hours of notice and all other repairs within 14 days. If Landlord fails to commence within those periods, Tenant may, after a second written notice, cause the repair to be made and deduct the reasonable cost, not exceeding one month's rent in any twelve-month period, from the next installment. Nothing in this Rider waives the implied warranty of habitability.

sections.heading: RIDER C — SECURITY DEPOSIT
sections.text: Landlord holds the sum of $2,800 as security for Tenant's performance. The deposit shall be held in a segregated interest-bearing account at a federally insured institution located within this State. Within 30 days after surrender of the Premises, Landlord shall return the deposit together with accrued interest, less any lawful deductions, accompanied by an itemized written statement identifying each deduction and attaching supporting invoices. Failure to furnish the itemized statement within that period forfeits Landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 15 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Elmsworth County, Westmarch, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 15 days of recording.
